oneOf.description:
A repository or mirror describing a vendor's artifacts on the
vendor's behalf, having checked whatever evidence the vendor gave.

Bin.description:
An executable inside an artifact. Serialises as the bare path when the
PATH name is the file's own name, else as `{ "path", "name" }`.

RequiredBin.description: A command an executable needs on PATH.

min.description:
The lowest version that works, compared numerically by dot-separated
components with missing components padded with zero: `17` means
17.0.0 and later, including 21. Unrecognized spellings are unchecked.

name.description:
The name as the executable invokes it, bare: `java`, `python3`,
`git`. No directory and no `.exe`.

Requires.description:
What the host must already provide, by names the operating system
defines, so a consumer can check before installing. Nothing here names
another project or where to get it; see the specification's Host
requirements section.

bin.description:
Commands the executables run and cannot work without, by the bare
name on PATH, with an optional minimum version. Declared by the
vendor.

glibc_min.description: Minimum glibc for a `gnu` Linux build, such as `2.31`.

libs.description:
Shared libraries the executables load from the host, by the name
the loader resolves: a soname (`libssl.so.3`), a DLL name
(`vcruntime140.dll`), or a dylib name (`libssl.3.dylib`). Excludes
the C runtime baseline that `libc` and `glibc_min` cover and any
library the artifact ships itself. `packslip create` reads it from
the executables; an empty list means they were read and need
nothing, an absent one that nothing was checked.

os_min.description:
Minimum OS version, in the OS's own terms: `12` for macOS Monterey,
`10.0.17763` for Windows.

oneOf.description:
A sigstore bundle signed keylessly with a workload or human OIDC
identity, certified by Fulcio and logged to Rekor.

A sigstore bundle signed with a long-lived Ed25519 key, logged to
Rekor.

VerifiedArtifact.description:
An artifact the verified statement lists, with the digest the statement
signs for it.

arch.description:
`x86_64`, `aarch64`, `armv7`, `armv6`, `riscv64`, `i686`,
`powerpc64le`, `s390x`, `loongarch64`. Absent when the artifact
runs on any architecture.

bin.description:
Executables inside the artifact, as paths relative to the archive
root, or the artifact's own name (minus any compression suffix)
when it is a bare executable. A consumer puts these on PATH under
`name`.

extensions.description:
Vendor- or consumer-defined data about this artifact. See
[`Extensions`].

format.description:
The archive type (`tar.xz`, `tar.gz`, `tar.zst`, `tar.bz2`, `tgz`,
`tar`, `zip`, `7z`), a single compressed executable (`gz`, `xz`,
`zst`, `bz2`), an installer (`deb`, `rpm`, `dmg`, `pkg`, `msi`,
`msix`, `exe`, `appimage`), or `raw` for a bare executable. Two
artifacts that differ only in format carry the same build, and a
consumer takes whichever it prefers. Required: an artifact whose
format is unknown is one no consumer can select.

`Option` so that a document leaving it out still parses and is
then refused by `validate`, which can name the artifact. The field
is not optional: no `serde(default)`, so the schema demands it.

libc.description:
`gnu` or `musl`, for a Linux build. Absent when the artifact does
not depend on one.

os.description:
`linux`, `darwin`, `windows`, `freebsd`, `netbsd`, `openbsd`,
`illumos`, `android`, `ios`. Absent when the artifact runs on any
OS.

provenance.description: URLs of build provenance statements (SLSA) for this artifact.

requires.description: What the artifact needs from the host.

sha256.description: The signed SHA-256 of the file, in lowercase hex.

variant.description:
Tells apart builds that share os, arch, and libc: `fips`,
`baseline`, `debug`, `installer`, `source`. A consumer selects only
artifacts without a variant unless asked for one.

artifacts.description:
Every artifact the statement lists, in document order, with its
signed digest. Whatever the caller passed as `--artifact`, these are
verified metadata: nothing was downloaded to produce them.

asset_count.description: How many assets the document lists besides its artifacts.

attested_by.description: Whether the vendor or a repackager made the claim.

channel.description: The channel the version's prerelease part names, if any.

checked_artifacts.description: Artifacts whose digests were checked against files.

checked_assets.description:
Resource assets, such as an SBOM or a skill archive, whose digests
were checked against files.

key_id.description: Who signed: the certificate identity, or the key id.

logged_at.description:
When the transparency log recorded the signature, RFC 3339. None
only for an unlogged bundle the consumer chose to accept.

pin_workflow.description:
Whether the document asks consumers to hold later releases to the
workflow that signed it. See [`crate::model::Identity::pin_workflow`].

prerelease.description: Whether the version has a prerelease part.

provenance_linked.description:
Whether every artifact links build provenance for the consumer to
verify. The packslip proves the manifest; SLSA provenance, if
verified, proves the build.

requires.description:
What each artifact requires of the host, one line per artifact
that declares anything: `name: glibc>=2.31; libs libz.so.1; bin
java>=17`.

resources.description:
The kinds of resources declared (completions, man pages, CLI
specs, ...), one label per entry, in document order.
